title: MAGNET OF LOVE: The Unburned Child of Cebu’s Heart
explanation: Devotional images and religious artifacts often acquire meaning through stories of survival, miracles, fire, disaster, or protection. Cebu’s religious identity is deeply connected to the Santo Niño, whose image functions not only as an object of worship but as a symbol of local history, colonial encounter, family devotion, and civic identity. Stories surrounding sacred objects should be distinguished between documented history, tradition, and faith claims.
why: Religious heritage shapes festivals, tourism, community memory, and personal identity. Understanding both history and belief allows respectful discussion without confusing devotion with historical proof.

title: 99 Years of Land, But for Whom?
explanation: Proposals allowing longer land leases or changing rules around foreign use of land raise questions about investment, sovereignty, housing, agriculture, and who ultimately benefits from development. Long leases can attract capital while functioning economically much like ownership over a person’s lifetime. Policy therefore needs safeguards for food security, local communities, land prices, and strategic assets.
why: Land is scarce and politically sensitive. Rules that affect control of land can influence housing affordability, farming, indigenous rights, and the distribution of economic gains.

title: Power Struggle for Hezbollah: Leader Assassinated
explanation: The killing of a senior leader of an armed political organization can disrupt command structures, trigger retaliation, and reshape regional alliances. Hezbollah is both a Lebanese political actor and an armed group deeply connected to Iran and conflict with Israel. Leadership decapitation does not automatically end an organization; succession, ideology, funding, and local support matter.
why: Escalation in the Middle East can affect OFWs, oil prices, shipping, and diplomatic evacuation operations. Regional conflict has direct economic and human consequences for the Philippines.

title: Uganda’s orphanage crisis and the fight for children’s futures
explanation: Institutional orphanages can provide emergency shelter but may also create long-term developmental problems when children grow up without stable family relationships. Global child-welfare policy increasingly favors family-based care, kinship care, foster systems, and community support where safe. Not all children in orphanages are legally orphaned; poverty may separate families that could remain together with adequate assistance.
why: The Philippines also faces child abandonment, institutional care, adoption, and poverty-related family separation. International lessons can inform stronger family-based protection systems.

title: EXPLAINER | Pearls of Controversy: Breaking the Shell of Injustice in Bugsuk, Palawan
explanation: Development and land disputes in Palawan often involve competing claims among indigenous communities, private interests, tourism, agriculture, conservation, and government agencies. In places such as Bugsuk, the key issues include ancestral-domain recognition, meaningful consent, historical possession, and whether communities benefit from or are displaced by development.
why: Palawan is both ecologically valuable and economically attractive. Protecting indigenous land rights tests whether development can proceed without erasing communities that have lived on the land for generations.

title: FAITH IN MOTION: Honoring the Black Nazarene with devotion
explanation: The Feast of the Black Nazarene and the Traslación bring together millions of devotees who express faith through procession, prayer, sacrifice, touching the image or ropes, and fulfillment of panata. The devotion reflects Catholic history, popular religiosity, collective identity, and the human search for hope amid hardship. Large gatherings also require major public-safety, health, and crowd-management systems.
why: The devotion is one of the country’s largest expressions of popular faith. It shows how religion, urban governance, culture, and public safety intersect.

title: Creating Tax Reforms towards Business and Economic Recovery in the Philippines
explanation: Tax reform tries to raise enough revenue for government while keeping the economy competitive and encouraging investment. Changes to corporate income tax, incentives, deductions, or compliance rules can help businesses expand, but poorly targeted incentives can reduce revenue without producing enough jobs. The quality of reform depends on simplicity, fairness, predictability, and measurable economic benefit.
why: Tax policy affects employment, prices, public services, and government borrowing. Business-friendly rules are valuable only when economic gains are broadly shared.

title: Reality Check: The Philippines’ Struggle to Achieve Sustainable Development Goals
explanation: The Sustainable Development Goals cover poverty, hunger, health, education, gender equality, water, energy, decent work, climate, institutions, and other interconnected targets. Progress can be uneven: improvement in one indicator may coexist with setbacks elsewhere. National averages can also hide regional and class inequality.
why: The SDGs provide a framework for judging whether growth translates into real improvements in people’s lives. They help move debate beyond GDP alone.

title: A BUDGET BATTLE: Who Wins, Who Loses, and Who Pays the Price?
explanation: National budgets reveal political priorities because every increase for one program competes with other needs under limited resources. Cuts to education, health, agriculture, infrastructure, social protection, or research can have long-term consequences, while debt service and mandatory spending reduce flexibility. The key is not only the headline amount but where funds move and whether agencies can spend them effectively.
why: Budgets determine classrooms, hospitals, roads, subsidies, salaries, and local services. Citizens should treat budget debates as decisions about daily life, not technical accounting.

title: EXPLAINER | Expanding prescriptive protections
explanation: Changes in who may prescribe, dispense, or provide certain medicines can expand healthcare access, especially where doctors are scarce. But expanding authority requires training, clear scopes of practice, referral rules, recordkeeping, and patient-safety safeguards. Access and quality should advance together.
why: Rural and underserved communities often face health-worker shortages. Carefully designed task-sharing can improve access without lowering standards.

title: The United States-Philippines alliance’s prospects after the US election
explanation: Philippine security cooperation with the United States is shaped by treaties, defense agreements, bases access, military exercises, domestic politics, and each American administration’s regional strategy. A change in U.S. leadership can affect rhetoric, spending, China policy, and alliance priorities, but formal agreements create continuity beyond one president.
why: U.S. policy influences deterrence in the West Philippine Sea, military modernization, trade, migration, and regional stability. The Philippines must protect its interests regardless of who occupies the White House.

title: 2024 Wrapped: When chaos, corruption, and climate crises ravaged the Philippines
explanation: A year-end political and social review helps connect events that may otherwise feel isolated: storms, heat, governance controversies, inflation, corruption allegations, transport problems, and institutional conflict. The value of a “wrapped” format is not simply remembering headlines but asking what patterns persisted and which problems were left unresolved.
why: National memory is short when news cycles move quickly. Annual synthesis helps citizens evaluate whether crises were exceptional events or symptoms of deeper systems.

title: #Unwrapped: What went wrong with 2024 Spotify Wrapped?
explanation: Spotify Wrapped is both a personalized product feature and one of the world’s most successful annual marketing campaigns. When users perceive the output as less accurate, creative, or emotionally resonant, the disappointment reveals how much trust people place in algorithmic personalization. A data product succeeds not only when calculations are correct but when users recognize themselves in the result.
why: Digital platforms increasingly shape entertainment and identity. Understanding personalization helps users think critically about what platforms know, infer, and choose to show them.

title: EXPLAINER | Behind Bars for a Decade: Mary Jane Veloso’s Journey
explanation: Mary Jane Veloso’s case became a major issue involving labor migration, human trafficking allegations, drug laws, consular assistance, death-penalty policy, and Philippine-Indonesian diplomacy. Her experience illustrates how vulnerable migrant workers can be recruited through informal networks and placed at extraordinary legal risk abroad.
why: Millions seek work overseas. Strong recruitment regulation, legal assistance, trafficking prevention, and migrant-worker education can be the difference between opportunity and catastrophe.

title: EXPLAINER | A nation divided: Marcos and Duterte battle on issues of governance
explanation: Political alliances in the Philippines can fracture when competing families, succession plans, policy disagreements, investigations, and control of institutions create conflicting incentives. The Marcos-Duterte split illustrates how electoral unity does not necessarily mean a shared governing ideology. Once alliances break, government decisions can become intertwined with preparation for the next election.
why: Elite conflict can affect budgets, appointments, legislation, investigations, and public trust. Citizens should judge each side on evidence and governance, not inherited loyalty.

title: EXPLAINER | The Philippines at Frontlines: Climate change mitigation through policies and actions
explanation: Climate policy has two major dimensions: mitigation, which reduces greenhouse-gas emissions, and adaptation, which reduces harm from climate impacts. The Philippines contributes a relatively small share of global emissions but is highly vulnerable, creating a strong interest in renewable energy, resilient infrastructure, climate finance, forest protection, and international accountability.
why: Climate change affects food, water, heat, storms, coasts, health, and livelihoods. The country needs both global emissions cuts and local resilience.

title: EXPLAINER | The consequence of inaction: grounds for Vice President impeachment
explanation: Impeachment complaints can involve alleged acts as well as failures to act when a constitutional officer has a legal duty. Whether inaction qualifies as an impeachable offense depends on the specific allegation, evidence, constitutional ground, and connection to public trust or culpable violation. Political criticism alone is not enough; legal standards still matter.
why: Accountability includes how officials use power and how they fail to use it. Understanding the distinction helps citizens evaluate charges more rigorously.

title: EXPLAINER | Collateral Murder: The political disputes of the Iranian-Israeli
explanation: Iran-Israel conflict combines state rivalry, nuclear concerns, proxy forces, targeted killings, airstrikes, and competing security doctrines. Civilian casualties become central because military actions can have consequences far beyond intended targets. International humanitarian law focuses on distinction, proportionality, and precautions in attack.
why: Escalation affects global fuel costs and Filipinos living or working across the Middle East. It also tests international rules the Philippines relies on in its own security disputes.

title: EXPLAINER | Supreme Court simplifies recognition of foreign divorce
explanation: Philippine law generally does not provide domestic absolute divorce for Filipino couples, but foreign divorces involving a foreign spouse can sometimes be recognized under legal rules. Court decisions that simplify proof or recognition procedures can reduce cost and uncertainty for affected Filipinos. The details depend on the foreign law, decree, marriage circumstances, and evidence presented.
why: Many Filipinos marry foreign nationals or migrate abroad. Clear recognition rules affect civil status, remarriage, property, inheritance, and family stability.

title: EXPLAINER | Language at the crossroads: Unpacking the Shift in Language Policy
explanation: Mother-tongue education aims to build early learning using a language children understand well, but implementation can be difficult when classrooms are multilingual, materials are scarce, or teachers lack training. Policy shifts should distinguish problems in design from problems in execution and consider evidence on literacy transfer to Filipino and English.
why: Language policy directly affects whether children understand their earliest lessons. It also influences the survival and status of regional languages.

title: EXPLAINER | The Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act: A Response to Agricultural Issues
explanation: Agricultural economic sabotage laws target large-scale smuggling, hoarding, profiteering, and cartel-like behavior that can distort food prices and hurt farmers. Strong penalties may deter organized abuse, but enforcement depends on customs data, market monitoring, prosecution, and protection against selective application. Criminal law cannot by itself fix weak farm productivity or logistics.
why: Food prices are a major household concern. Protecting farmers and consumers requires both anti-smuggling enforcement and long-term agricultural reform.

title: EXPLAINER | Rice without roots: How the Philippines Became the World’s Top Rice Importer
explanation: Rice imports rise when domestic production cannot meet consumption at competitive prices or when government uses imports to stabilize supply. Causes can include farm size, irrigation, climate shocks, input costs, mechanization, post-harvest losses, trade policy, and population demand. Import dependence is not simply proof that farmers failed; it reflects the whole agricultural system.
why: Rice is a staple and a politically sensitive commodity. Policy must balance affordable consumer prices with sustainable farmer incomes and food security.

title: EXPLAINER | Root out: COMELEC combats the roots of disinformation in digital campaigning for 2025 Philippine elections
explanation: Election disinformation can involve fake accounts, manipulated media, false endorsements, coordinated networks, undeclared advertising, and deceptive campaign content. Election regulators can require disclosures and set rules, but enforcement is difficult when content spreads across platforms and jurisdictions. Cooperation with media, civil society, and technology companies is necessary.
why: False political information can distort voter choice before corrections catch up. Transparent digital campaigning is essential to credible elections.

title: EXPLAINER | The plight of Southern Palawan indigenous people to reclaim ancestral land
explanation: Indigenous land claims depend on historical occupation, customary law, ancestral-domain processes, maps, state titles, and sometimes decades of conflict with private or government claims. Legal recognition can take years even when communities have long-standing cultural ties to the land.
why: Ancestral-domain rights test whether the state recognizes histories that predate modern property documents. Delayed justice can permanently alter communities and ecosystems.

title: EXPLAINER | Swerving paths to decongested roads
explanation: Traffic cannot be solved sustainably by adding road space alone because new capacity can encourage more driving. Effective mobility combines reliable public transport, walkability, cycling, road pricing or parking management, land-use planning, freight management, and better intersections. The objective is moving people efficiently, not simply moving more cars.
why: Congestion wastes hours, fuel, productivity, and family time. Transport reform is an economic and quality-of-life priority.
